source.title: DELTA-Code: How Does RL Unlock and Transfer New Programming Algorithms in LLMs?
source.authors: Yi-You Sun; Yuhan Cao; Pohao Huang; Hao-Yue Bai; Hanna Hajishirzi; Nouha Dziri; D. Song

record.tranche_reason: The study examines grokking-like transitions during RL fine-tuning of LLMs on coding tasks, extending the phenomenon to a new setting. Its reported curves primarily measure training-set full-pass performance, not the delayed test-accuracy pattern specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports RL training dynamics and post-training transfer results. Its phase-transition curves are described as training-data full-pass rates; it does not report test accuracy rising after a period of saturated training accuracy, or a sweep showing that smaller training sets take longer. Results cited from prior work are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper calls its RL training curves 'grokking', but they show a different construct. Training-data full-pass reward stays near zero during a sparse-reward exploration plateau, then jumps. No version's pattern is measured: test accuracy rising long after training accuracy has saturated. Training and test performance are never shown to diverge. The tasks are synthetic generated coding families, not realistic pretraining or fine-tuning data, so V4 is not tested either. The finding belongs under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also frame the abrupt training-reward transition as evidence that RL can discover strategies beyond the base model (pass@128 = 0 to 100% on HAS), against the view that RL only sharpens existing skills. They say which outcome occurs depends on reward design, data mix, task hardness and recipe.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses RL fine-tuning of instruction-tuned LLMs on generated coding and simulation tasks, with full-pass or per-test rewards. It does not use the original small-network supervised algorithmic-data setup or measure its training-set-size delay relationship.
record.method_sensitivity: Reward schedule, curriculum-family compatibility, experience replay, feedback-in-the-loop, task family and difficulty, model family and scale, and continued training (which can lead to RL collapse).

fits_no_version.finding: Under GRPO on hard synthetic coding families, training full-pass reward stays near zero for hundreds of steps, then rises abruptly to near-perfect. Dense-reward warm-up enables this on HAS but not on PREPEND. The pattern recurs on REGEX, BouncingSim and Nemotron-14B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In RL fine-tuning of LLMs with sparse verifiable rewards, training reward can show a long exploration plateau followed by an abrupt transition. This depends on reward schedule, task difficulty and curriculum compatibility.

fits_no_version.finding: After RL on Basic BouncingSim, transfer is strong in-distribution and on compositional cases (60–70%). It declines with difficulty and is near zero on transformative cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RL-acquired coding skills transfer to parametric and compositional shifts but not to qualitatively new solution schemas.

record.problems: The main phase-transition evidence is described as training-data full-pass performance, so it does not establish delayed test generalization. Several training-curve results are qualitative, and the paper reports averages over 4 runs without error bars or other uncertainty measures in the provided text.

untested.parts: No small networks on small algorithmic datasets; no train-saturated/test-delayed curve; no training-set-size sweep.
No circuit analysis or continuous progress measures.
No initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation; no lazy-to-rich test.
Synthetic generated coding tasks rather than realistic data. The delay is in training reward, not in generalization after training saturates.
No weight decay, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
Learned algorithms are not compared across runs.

record.verdict_notes: The paper uses 'grokking' for a sparse-reward exploration-then-convergence transition in training reward. That is not the memorize-then-generalize gap the versions describe. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. No uncertainty is reported beyond averaging over 4 runs.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test small networks trained on small algorithmic datasets, delayed test accuracy after training accuracy saturates, or whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
No mechanistic circuit formation, memorizing-component removal, or continuous circuit progress measure is reported.
No image, text, or molecule training comparison, initialization-scale sweep, weight-norm intervention, or lazy-to-rich transition test is reported.
The study does fine-tune LLMs with RL, but its controlled/generated coding tasks do not test delayed generalization during pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic training data.
No weight-decay or low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset-size prediction, or ungrokking test is reported.
The study does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifact control is reported.

conditions.value: per-test pass rate, then full pass

rows.baseline: 0% full pass rate at pass@128 for the reference model
rows.value: 100% full pass rate after staged RL
rows.note: The reference-model result and post-RL full-pass result are reported; this comparison does not give a delayed test-accuracy trajectory.
rows.check: Before/after pass@k comparison on HAS (Figure 4) with no timing relative to training saturation. Correctly unlinked.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507
rows.operation_detail: GRPO using per-test pass rate throughout
rows.value: Per-test reward quickly saturates after ∼100 steps; full-pass rate remains <0.01%
rows.note: The dense reward provides initial traction but does not produce meaningful full-pass performance in this setup.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507
rows.operation_detail: Per-test pass-rate warm-up followed by binary full-pass RL

conditions.value: per-test pass rate, then full pass

rows.baseline: Full-pass rate remains <1% during the reported ∼450-step exploration phase
rows.value: After a sudden grokking moment, performance converges to near-perfect; nearly a 100% absolute improvement in pass@k versus the reference model
rows.note: The reported phase transition is a training performance result; the text does not establish a corresponding delayed test-accuracy curve.
rows.check: The jump is in training reward after a near-zero plateau, not delayed generalization after training saturation. The text's figure references for 5(a)/(b)/(c) are inconsistent with the caption; the reader's locator is acceptable.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507
rows.operation_detail: Experience replay of successful traces during RL

conditions.value: Up to three most recent successful traces appended when the same query reappears

rows.value: Experience replay helps the model grok earlier, but convergence is still slower than baseline GRPO
rows.note: The comparison is described qualitatively; no exact step values are stated.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507
rows.operation_detail: Experience replay with verifier feedback injected into generation

conditions.value: Failure feedback replaces EOS once and generation continues

rows.value: Applying feedback-in-the-loop once expedites the grokking moment but reduces training stability
rows.note: The authors report a faster transition alongside a stability cost.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507
rows.operation_detail: Curriculum through START/APPEND/EXACT, then REGEX, then target HAS
rows.value: REGEX curriculum leads to successful transfer and near-complete mastery of HAS at the final RL stage
rows.note: The result is attributed to structural compatibility between REGEX and HAS.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507
rows.operation_detail: Curriculum through START/APPEND/EXACT, then COMPR, then target HAS
rows.value: COMPR curriculum fails to progress beyond low pass rates on HAS
rows.note: The study says the curriculum outcome differs despite similar difficulty levels of the intermediate families.
rows.check: COMPR curriculum 'fails to progress beyond low pass rates'. This is failure to learn the target, better recorded as absent than partial; no number is given.
